utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. May we please hear the case number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And today's appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian and Michael McVicker with Lise-lotte Karlsson for the Office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic assisted by Mr. Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We may proceed immediately with the continuation of the cross-examination until 9.40, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something about the year 1991, that is September 1991. Do you know that the ruling SDA party in Prijedor did not permit the recruiting commission to inspect the lists of the military commissions?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me clarify this. In 1991, the Serbian Democratic Party acting -- acting apart from the legally elected authorities in the municipalities of Prijedor recommended to Serb military conscripts to volunteer, as they said, but not to report to the Secretariat for National Defence. Instead, they were to report to the barracks in Prijedor, put on a uniform, and go to fight in Croatia. The highest organs of government, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and other republic institutions explained that Bosniaks, Muslims, and others should not be taken in by the Serb propaganda and that they were not duty-bound to report and to put on uniforms and go to fight in Croatia. To make things even more absurd, at the head of the secretariat for National Defence, Becir Medunjanin had been appointed in a legal and regular way. He was a member of the Party of Democratic Action. But the military command took advantage of this, the military command from Prijedor, that is, headed by Vladimir Lasic, and Radmilo Zeljaja and they staged an incident or, rather, they attempted to break into the secretariat for National Defence by force and take away the list with the names of all men liable for military service in the municipality of Prijedor. In other words, Becir Medunjanin, as the secretary of the military department in Prijedor was quite right. He was obeying instructions coming from Sarajevo, from high authority, and he was right not to give Radomir Lasic, Zeljaja and their associates to take by force the lists of men liable for military service in the municipality of Prijedor. Let me explain. Let me explain why they needed those lists. Later on in 1992 when the Serb Democratic Party with the help of the army and police took over power in Prijedor, they made use of these lists to accuse all those who had not reported -- who had not responded to the call-up and accepted the Serb ideology and gone to fight in Slavonia, in Lipik and Pakrac, and also other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. All those who refused to join the Serb army who were Muslims and Croats were accused chiefly of this. This was one of the chief allegations made against them, one of the main reasons for their being taken to the camps, to Omarska and Keraterm. I will give you just one example. Stjepan Maric, an engineer, a Croat who was the director of the electronic mathematical centre in the Ljubija mines, although he was a Croat, was mobilised by force as an expert on rocket systems, and he was taken off to the war theatre in Croatia. He spent a certain time in Croatia at the war theatre but managed to escape from there. He didn't want to kill his own people, the Croatian people. Stjepan Maric was one of the first people to be taken to the Omarska camp, and he was killed in July 1992, although for a time he obediently served in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May we conclude that your answer to my question is yes?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The legal authorities did not allow the paramilitary formations led by Zeljaja and Arsic to get hold of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that in 1991, in September, the JNA was a paramilitary formation in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it was taken on the character or, rather, already had taken on the character of a single-nation army, and it included a large number of paramilitary formations which they had under their control. They were arming them. They were giving them uniforms, not to go into further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your television company, from the beginning of September 1991, did it tell you, when you were reporting on the JNA, to use the term "The former JNA"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All the journalists of Bosniak and Croatian nationality used this term. Only the Serbian journalists still called it the Yugoslav Army, the People's Army, which intervened between the opposing sides. However, the army had lost its former character. Unfortunately, it became a single-nation army and started killing their own people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, can the Serbs from Bosnia carry out aggression against Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs from Bosnia did carry out an aggression against Bosnia with the help of -- with the help of their brothers on the other side of the River Drina. It was not only Serbs from Bosnia who took part in the killing of Bosnia. It was also the regular units from the former Yugoslavia or, rather, from Serbia. So that in the area of Prijedor and the Bosnian Krajina in 1992 there were parts of the Uzice Corps, the Knin Corps, and other smaller elite units which had arrived there in order to destroy Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who commanded them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their Commander-in-Chief is now here in Scheveningen, and he is being tried. I'm referring to Slobodan Milosevic. And those who implemented his policy in Bosnia and Herzegovina are the most wanted men; they are Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you speak of the percentage of voters who voted for an independent Bosnia at the referendum, do you know what percentage of Serbs voted for an independent Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but according to what I can remember of what I reported from the referendum, I think that according to the statements made by members of the electoral commissions I visited and I had an opportunity to visit only a few polling stations, a large number of Serbs voted for an independent and sovereign Bosnia. How many Serbs actually voted for an independent and sovereign Bosnia we can only speculate, because it is the right of every voter to vote in secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Croatian villages in the Ljubija hinterland were armed, how well they were armed, and whether they obtained weapons from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian villages in the hinterland of Ljubija where the Croatian Democratic Union was in power were armed but very poorly armed. I have already said here that the Muslims and the Croats in the municipality of Prijedor stood no chance. And the same applies to the whole of the Bosnian Krajina. The area of Prijedor and Banja Luka, I will repeat, was the largest military barracks in Europe, where there was a concentration of large rocket systems. There was a large number of soldiers of the former Yugoslav army who had retreated from Slovenia and Croatia and the most elite units were there. So that the Muslims and Croats in the area of the Bosnian Krajina stood no chance. The weapons the Croats in the Ljubija hinterland and the Muslims in Kozarac had managed to collect were very meager. They were very -- they were very badly armed in comparison to the Serbian army and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in March 1992 the villages of Donja Puharska were already holding night patrols?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the decision of the executive board of the legally elected municipal assembly, the citizens of Prijedor in the enclaves where Muslims mostly lived were very upset because of frequent incursions by rampaging drunken Serbian soldiers who, as I said, were stationed in Prijedor and its surroundings. They would get drunk at night and enter parts of town inhabited by Muslims or Croats. They would fire shots. They would shout threats. They would provoke people. And as far as I can remember, at one of the sessions of the then-legally elected municipal assembly, a decision was made that the local communes inhabited mostly by non-Serbs should set up patrols consisting of two or three men or set up checkpoints where they could at least report when a group of Serbian soldiers turned up so that someone could come from the main police station and try to calm down the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is your answer to my question yes?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But these checkpoints were not of a militant character. It was simply to control who entered into the Muslim enclaves, into their depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In March 1992, was there anarchy, smuggling, corruption in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my previous testimony, I have already explained the political atmosphere in the municipality of Prijedor in early 1992. This same situation obtained in 1991 as well. The Prijedor Municipal Assembly was a legal body composed of about 30 delegates of the Party of Democratic Action, 28 from the Serbian Democratic Party while the others were deputies from other parties, and it was unable to reach a single decision which was vital for the citizens of Prijedor only because in making any decision, the work of the assembly was obstructed by members of the party of the Serbian Democratic Party who in this way obstructed any decision being reached including legislation important for the life of a town such as Prijedor. In this way, the Serbian deputies, by obstructing the work of the assembly, only wanted to gain time. They wanted nothing to get better in the municipality of Prijedor. And paradoxically, in the meantime, they worked on establishing parallel Serbian institutions, a Serbian army, a Serbian assembly, so that when they took power in late April 1992, they could level accusations at the Party of Democratic Action and others, saying that they were to blame for the fact that the Prijedor municipality had gone from bad to worse. Let me just tell you. After the national parties came to power, only the leading posts were assigned in the municipality of Prijedor. All the other posts and key positions in Prijedor organisations, companies, and so on were never assigned. And one of the reasons for this was that this was obstructed by the Serbian side. Ninety-five per cent of the men in these leading posts were Serbs from the former system. And as I said, it was not important whether someone had a membership card of the Serbian Democratic Party. They all worked in a concerted manner on making Prijedor an ethnically pure town and on having the other ethnic groups disappear from the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was a Crisis Staff established in Kozarac headed by Becir Medunjanin, in which Islam Bahonjic, Muta Tadic, Ilijaz Memic and Osman Didovic participated?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they saw what was happening in the other areas in Prijedor, I think the citizens, when they saw they had been abandoned by the Party of Democratic Action and its headquarters in Prijedor, a group of eminent citizens of Kozarac set up their own Crisis Staff which functioned very briefly. Unfortunately, they did try but it was too late. It was too late for them to organise. They bought some weapons or received some weapons, but the people of Kozarac never had a plan to attack any Serbian village, and Kozarac was surrounded by Serb villages. Their intention was only to try to defend their homes and their town should the Serbian army and police set out to destroy Kozarac and kill its people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Ljubija in May 1992, Branko Bjekic was exchanged. He was a police commander in Ljubija, a Croat by nationality. He was replaced by Fikret Sarajlic who had been dismissed from his job in Prijedor, and he was assisted by Drago Tokmadzic, Ismet Taric, Aziz Aliskovic and Velid Krupic. In this way, they took over the police station in Ljubija. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a very short time. They did not agree to be commanded by Simo Drljaca, and the extremists from the Serbian Democratic Party who had taken over the police station in Prijedor. Let me just mention to Their Honours that all the members of the Crisis Staff, the so-called Crisis Staff of Kozarac and these policemen headed by Fikret Sarajlic who took over the police station in Ljubija for only a few days, they were all killed in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your cousin Adnan took packages to Slavko Ecimovic at Krumovo or he sent them by Dr. Esad and Hamed Cuk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is. My cousin Adnan was a school friend of Slavko Ecimovic. They had gone to high school together. Slavko Ecimovic was the best man at my cousin Adnan's wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, how many detainees were there in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got there, there were about 5.000 people, because the elementary school which made part of that camp was full. The cooperative centre with the large cinema hall was overcrowded, and there were also other places. There is no need for me to explain it. It doesn't really matter. But the largest number of the inmates were in the Trnopolje camp under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Technical problems. There is a noise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now. The largest number of inmates in the Trnopolje camp were in the open air, in some shelters they made themselves of sticks and plastic bags and blankets to protect them from rain or sun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Kurevo units were divided in four parts, that the first one was headed by Kajmo Alagic and that his group was in the Ljubija area, that captain Suad Halilovic was also in that group? The second group who -- which had Slavko Ecimovic at its head, was in the area of Zagar, Polje, Tukovi and Prijedor. The third group headed by Lieutenant Asmir Muhic was responsible for the area of Rizvanovici, Hambarine, and Biscani. The fourth group with Iset Mesic, nicknamed Hadzija, at its head and Nenad Babic was in the area of Skela, Rasovci, and Puharska are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment because I have some technical problems. There, now it's better. Mr. Lukic, what you have just said in your rather exhaustive question is information which is not supported by any documents. This information about these groups has been taken from newspapers such as Kozarski Vjesnik, and this was written by Zivko Ecimovic and Rade Mutic a year after the power was taken, was seized in Prijedor. So the information that you have given us now come from the well-known kitchen of Zivko Ecimovic and Rade Mutic, and how relevant and how realistic it all is up to you to decide. If you want me to, I have a copy of Kozarski Vjesnik with this article and I can give it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One microphone is on, but the other one -- yes. Now we have two microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes it's on purpose that only one is on because we have some impacts on the clear line. What we heard before was already the line from Banja Luka. I just wanted to come back. You said just a minute before that "If you want me to, I have a copy of Kozarski Vjesnik with this article and I can give it to you." Please feel free to do so after the break this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do it in the afternoon, not before that, because excerpts from Kozarski Vjesnik are in my room here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information I have is that the facts were taken over from Mirza's diary who participated in the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is not the testimony. There is no question before the witness at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever read Mirza's diary? And Mirza participated in the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza, and the initial B, is an old acquaintance of mine from Prijedor, and he participated in the liberation of Prijedor in the same group as Slavko Ecimovic. And some fragments of his impressions about the event he told me, and I used them and included them in my book. But let me ask you something, Mr. Lukic. Who did you get my book from?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am not allowed to testify from the place that I am at.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my apologies. But if the subject about today's hearing is my book, then I object. My book is not a document nor does it have any archival value. My book was written for the public. And in view of the profit and everything else that the publishers are taking care of, some parts of my book were paraphrased without my knowledge, and I do not think that my book is relevant here to be discussed here. As far as I can see, all your questions actually arise from my book. But this is neither a literary club nor a discussion about -- about a book. And you are not -- you are neither a literary critic nor an historian to judge my book. I am quite ready to, in a regular procedure, in a civil action, to account for all that I've put in my book before a normal court, including Republika Srpska if it proved that it is impartial. And all those who are mentioned in the book, if they think that I was not right to do that, why don't they bring charges against me? As far as I know, I didn't present my book to the gentlemen from the OTP and the Tribunal to use it when writing the indictment against your client. I own up only to these statements that I gave to the representatives of the OTP of The Hague Tribunal and the statement that I signed, and I think you should leave the book for some other time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me ask the parties to refrain from discussing literature. It's on purpose that we have the witness before us, and the purpose is that we hear directly from him what he experienced to the best his recollection and not to go to third or secondary sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, hearsay is allowed in front of this Tribunal. This Defence would like to exclude that kind of evidence, and if it's the case, we would refrain from these line of questions, but unfortunately it's not. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with hearsay, to be quite clear. The witness was confronted with a line of questions on all these issues, and he answered in an adequate way, and I can see no merits to come back to what I would call not hearsay but secondary sources. Otherwise, we could read the book of the witness here and it would not be necessary to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm doing. I never mentioned his book. I used his book only to know and suppose what the witness could know. If he does not know, he can say so. I have to have some kind of source about the knowledge of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's right, but unfortunately, I can't here go back to this part where you started, "Did you read this or that book," and this is the way the question I would not admit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you aware who, on the 23rd of May, 1992, broadcast a message to the people of Hambarine to hand down their weapons?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was an ultimatum which was read by newscasters of Radio Prijedor on behalf of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor, Serb Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I should have known better already two minutes before it's 9.40, and we have to prepare --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have some bad news. I just received an e-mail that the satellite is down and we cannot get a videolink at the moment. I propose that we continue until we hear that the link is back up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you know that the OTP always has the best information available, so therefore, please continue. You let us know when it will be here, because we heard already the signals from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- I don't know if the video booth has different information. I'll ask my contact to send us an e-mail when they know otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videolink has the same information -- the video booth, excuse me, and they're trying right now to resolve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you say that Mile Mutic requested the surrender of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At some point, personally, the ultimatum to the people of Hambarine to surrender their weapons was issued directly by Mile Mutic, director of Kozarski Vjesnik and Radio Prijedor who, for a long time before that, already wore the uniform of the perished Yugoslav army with the high rank of the a major, I believe, a man who was trained at the reserve officer school in Bileca. And according to my sources, he was even a KOS man, that is, a man who was trained under the conditions of special war to take over the role in the media and to use these media to emit such ultimatums.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as for the front men of the SDA [Realtime transcript read in error "SDS"], where were they and their families when the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear. Oh, yes, I do. Mr. Lukic, let me make a brief introduction. In preparation for earlier cases, I had the opportunity -- I had the opportunity to get certain documents which concern Prijedor, and in a Radio Prijedor programme marking the third anniversary of the liberation of Prijedor - that is how the Serbs called it - when the 30th of May was proclaimed the most important holiday of the town, and that was the day when the ethnic cleansing began. The leader of this democratic party, Miskovic, said that when they launched the action on the 30th of April to take over the power, Mirza Mujadzic came to the barracks and had some talks there. Mirza Mujadzic went to the barracks to discuss with Simo Miskovic and Drago Zeljaja and others and other people who were to take over the power that night. And Simo Miskovic says openly, but he glassed in silence over the most important thing, where they had reached an understanding, that is to take the power without any bullet being fired, that is, without force. And then it is said that the problems arose only when they were discussing where to go to dinner after that. Mirza Mujadzic, after that, that is after the power was taken over, acting under the instructions of his friends in the SDS [As interpreted] went somewhere to Hambarine field, somewhere in the area of Carakovo where he spent -- spent some time. It is true that Dr. Mirza Mujadzic earlier, at the time when it was still possible, had sent his family somewhere outside Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think the question that was asked and that was answered was "the front men of the SDA," but the transcript showed that the transcript showed that the question said "SDS".

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification to the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say you were beaten in the Omarska camp. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. Not me only, everybody else too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened to your glasses as they beat you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not wear any glasses in the camp of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the dioptrics?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I think it's over plus five or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And at that time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was 0.75 plus 0.75. But I had glasses and I used glasses only when I dared use them because I was afraid, but as a rule I did not use them because I did not really need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you following the cases before the -- before the Tribunal and especially the cases relating to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the country that I live in, all I can do is keep up with agency news from the Milosevic case, that is, only Milosevic's trial is in the centre of attention. There is absolutely no information at all about other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are preparing a documentary film, and I presume that you see a lot of material in relation to that, do you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I'm still gathering the material. I have not yet embarked on that film. But I did -- but I recorded some of it myself, travelling around refugee camps in Bosnia, that is, those areas, those locations where the people from Prijedor still are. I also paid visits to Prijedorians who live abroad and also prepared some episodes about them. Perhaps I will use them in my documentary film that I will shoot some day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know when did Dr. Stakic start to grow his beard?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that is his personal private matter when he started growing a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you described him that he started growing a beard, that he put on weight, that he started growing older. Do you know when all that happened?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It was the first day when I came here for the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it is indeed a question the witness cannot answer, to refrain from other comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. Please receive my apologies if you found some of my questions disagreeable. Thank you very much. This is the end of my cross-examination, and I wish you a nice trip home whenever you live.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic, for your very correct examination. You're a professional, and I also wish you plenty of success in your further work in the defence of your client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are there any questions in re-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just learnt that there is a total breakdown of all the lines, and we have to proceed. What about the video prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't -- I've asked what the status is of the transcript. I believe by now we should have a transcript, although I haven't received an answer, in B/C/S. We probably do not yet have a translation, but if Your Honour wants to take a 15-minute break, I can come down. I think by then we will probably at least have a transcript in B/C/S for the booth. Your Honour may even want to take a longer break because I have to say that the sound quality, as Your Honours heard the first time, is actually much worse on the first portion of the videotape than it was during the interview of Dr. Stakic. I don't know if the interpreters want to hear it once in the booth, the tape, with the transcript before they do it in court in front of Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What is the intention? How many portions do you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There are three portions, a total of 15 minutes. And actually, I do not think it has to be shown in front of this witness. The witness may have some comments but it's a report by Mr. Mutic, I believe. Mr. Sivac has already stated that. And it speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But it may be of some assistance that the witness can give us one or other comment by his huge experience in this case. But then before we start with the break, I personally have only one question. Unfortunately, I haven't the transcript of yesterday already before me, but could -- from the top of my head, you mentioned yesterday in relation to one document, I think it was S243, on the destruction of some buildings that there are several false documents on the market, and it would be well known that indeed some documents are more or less fake and produced only later. You were not asked and therefore you did not comment on this. Could you please explain for our better understanding a little bit more what is this? Is it only a rumour or do you know that there are such falsifications of documents and done by whom and for what purpose? The background of this question is that it might be that in this concrete case we have to rely on numerous documents, documents where the authenticity is contested. And therefore, I would like you to explain to us something about your knowledge on this issue of alleged false documents.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, the knowledge that I have, and not only that I have but also the knowledge of the people who are currently in power in the municipality of Prijedor, shows that a large number -- a large portion of precisely cadastral books, land surveying books, and all the other property records which relate to the property in the municipality of Prijedor have been tampered with, have been changed. Some were forged. And all the documents which are issued by the municipal authorities in Prijedor need to be subjected to close scrutiny. When it took over the power, the Serb Democratic Party, one of the first things it did, was to take up some of the land surveying books and property records, was to change, to forge the books and records there regarding the owners. And people who go now there trying to re-enter their property, their ownership, are running into serious trouble now. That will be my answer. So I'd like to ask you to try to put all these documents in line with documents which perhaps could be obtained from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So what I understand from your question is that, first of all, these special kinds of cadastral books and land surveying books, they are the ones you had in mind when you discussed on the forgery of books and records or documents. Have you ever heard that there are other documents or even newspapers such as Kozarski Vjesnik or orders given by what kind of authority in the municipalities over or under the headline "Crisis Staff," or "War Presidency"? Have you ever heard that these documents were subject to forgery?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that, but I wish to draw your attention to a Kozarski Vjesnik issue, I'm not sure you're familiar with it, which featured a map. I think that this Kozarski Vjesnik issue is some time from April or March 1992. On that map, the Prijedor municipality is divided into its Serb part and its Muslim part. And in the accompanying text, it says that the Serbs own 70 per cent of the territory of the municipality of Prijedor. At that time already, they had turned to all the social ownership, including large parts of the national park of Kozara, large public farms. All the major companies, they simply said that all these companies should belong to the Serb people. And Muslims were given nothing. They were only given some small villages where Muslims, Bosniaks, and Croats used to constitute a majority population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. As mentioned before, we would appreciate if this afternoon you could bring along this article you mentioned before to court, and may I ask one additional question? You are --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the framework of your research, did you ever come into the possession of the Official Gazette number 1, 1992, of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Although through some of my private contacts I tried to obtain some sort of documentation on the basis of which I could make a film or write a new book. But what I was most interested in were the minutes or, rather, the records from the Omarska and Keraterm camps where inmates were interrogated and investigated. Through my friends who are living there, and for their safety, I must not mention their names. I tried to obtain one or more such records, but after all my attempts, I was told that all the documentations about the investigations carried out in the camps of Omarska and Keraterm were burnt very soon after the camps were closed down. So the records were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Judge Fassi Fihri, do you have any questions? No. Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in your testimony of 1994 you said, page 9 English version, at Serb meetings in Maricka, a village used by Chetniks as a base and where most of the guards at Omarska came from, people such as Radovan Karadzic and Jovan Raskovic from Knin and Krajisnik appeared and Chetniks wearing uniform caps with cockades and other insignia. Can you explain to us why this village or town became a base for Chetniks and the meetings of -- Serbian meetings?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are referring to the rally held in the village of Maricka in front of one of the oldest Orthodox churches in the area. This took place in August 1990 on a great Serbian holiday, Ilindan, Saint Eligus feast day. Maricka was not selected by chance. A month or more before this event took place, I was filming near this village, in another village called Nisivici. I was filming a ceremony in which - I don't know if this word can be translated or interpreted - but the foundations of a church destroyed in World War II were blessed or consecrated. This church had been destroyed by the Partisans, but it had been a Chetnik base during World War II. Fifty years later, the authorities in Prijedor allowed another church to be built on the same spot, and as early as that time, several months before this took place, it was already evident. There were improvised stalls around the church selling Chetnik insignia. Chetnik music was being played very loudly, over loudspeakers, and this was deeply offensive to all the other nations. And this was all done openly, not even trying to conceal it. I said that that area traditionally always nurtured the ideology of Draza Mihajlovic and his followers, that for 50 years their wish to continue along the lines put forward by their great leader, Draza Mihajlovic, they wanted to cleanse all the areas where they lived of Muslims and Croats. They wanted them to be purely Serb settlements. And as I wrote in one of my texts, the masks people wore were removed at that time. Things that had been long forgotten were brought out of the closet, and the symbols of the Chetnik movement, the kokarda, were resurrected. These places again became places where crimes could be committed, and I was proved to be right. Your Honour, Maricka was not selected by accident as one of the places where the long concealed tradition had been nurtured, where revenge had been planned for so long, where plans had been made that all non-Serbs should be killed. And as General Mladic later on said in an interview after the conquest of Srebrenica, after many, many years, we are revenged against the Turks, as they called us, for their uprising and for everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, have you any knowledge about Dr. Stakic's relationship with Radovan Karadzic and other leaders of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no evidence of this or any documents to prove it, but probably in view of his post, he would have to have had contacts because it was the policy of Radovan Karadzic and his associates that he so diligently implemented in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, in your statement in the framework of German participation in the UN Commission of Experts Prijedor Project, in March of 1994, you mentioned the name of Ranko Curcija as the member of Crisis Staff and said that he was also president of the radical Chetnik party. Can you tell us about this party and about the activity of this Serb Radical Party in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the name of this man is Ranko Curcija. He was a driving instructor in a driving school. For a very brief time in 1992, he was at the head of the Radical Party, as far as I know, in Prijedor, and he was a follower of the policy of his big idol Vojislav Seselj who he received very warmly in the town of Prijedor one day. A big rally of the Radical Party was held in the amateur theatre in Prijedor, and it was attended by their leader, Vojislav Seselj, in person. Ranko Curcija stayed in that position for a very short time because he was not suitable. The leadership of the Radical Party explained that Ranko Curcija was a Serb married to a Croatian woman and that it was unimaginable that the Radical Party could be led by a person who was married to a Croat and living with her. Ranko Curcija was replaced. As far as I know he was sent off to the battlefield somewhere as a punishment. And the post of the president of the Radical Party was filled by my colleague, a journalist and banker, Branko Maksimovic who was a correspondent of the Belgrade newspaper Politika from that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do you know other persons from the Prijedor municipality who participated in the activities of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do more or less. Branko Maksimovic's deputies were Kamenko Radzenovic [phoen], also known as the Colonel Pukovnik, Slavko Gavronovic who studied at university but never graduated. He was a student for over 30 years, and he was in the top leadership of the Serb Radical Party. There were the Sovin brothers. I would mention each of their names, who originate from an old Chetnik family and arrived in Prijedor from the area of Drvar. And there were many others whose names I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask to whom it may concern any news from Banja Luka? Any updates?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't have any, but I did find out that apparently our computers continue to be down today and our transcript will not be completed or hasn't been completed yet. It's still quite a ways to go, and I think it's a difficult tape. We probably want to do it right. I actually would prefer to do it right and I don't think it will be necessary to have the witness here because it is a news report. He didn't film it, and we have the reporter -- he has indicated that he recognised the reporter who was speaking, Mr. Mutic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've just been informed that the satellite system is still down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Nevertheless, may I ask whether it is possible to see the three portions after a break of half an hour and the OTP could provide the booths with these portions that they can see it in advance, that we at least have a slight impression? And the background is I want to avoid a situation that either the Judges or the Defence later states it's necessary to hear and to see this once again in the presence of the witness before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic is sick. He had a temperature yesterday and he has a temperature today. He only didn't want to complain because he understood that this witness has to leave and that the videolink has been prearranged in advance. But if the videolink is not likely to be successfully connected today, with the permission of Your Honours, we would like to have this -- today's session as short as possible so Mr. Stakic can try to recuperate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can I understand by commentaries that it's not your intention to request the witness to come a second time for the purposes of commentaries on the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not our intention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I indeed -- the only remaining question is that I would ask the witness to provide the article mentioned before during this day to a representative of the OTP and this later on can be forwarded to the Defence and the Judges. At the same time, I want to thank you, Mr. Sivac, very much for all your efforts to stand difficult questions from both parties, and I think you gave us an in-depth view into that what from your perspective happened at that time in Prijedor. And as I mentioned earlier, this is the only basis we have for exercising our mandate to come as close as possible to the truth on what has happened in Prijedor in 1992. Thank you very much. You are excused. And I may ask the usher to escort you from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the impression that everybody's already bored with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is indeed a wrong impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First of all, we have to take care of the health condition of the accused. May I ask that the nurse of this Tribunal takes contact with Dr. Stakic during the next break in order to find out whether or not he is able to follow the proceedings, because indeed we have to stand by, all participants, until we have the line, the connection, with Banja Luka. Everybody knows how expensive such videolink is, and it can't be substituted later. So therefore, we have to wait indeed until the link will be possible. And I would ask the Registry or the OTP, whoever knows first, to inform the other participants that we immediately re-assemble in the courtroom when we have the necessary information. May I turn to now what still has to be established. It's only very short. We did not decide on the admission into evidence of the video presented by Mr. Sivac. I understand the entire video is tendered by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The entire video that was played in court. I don't know if Your Honours want the entire video because that includes a lot of completely irrelevant information such as singing and a trip to Scandinavia by a group. I would at this time offer the section of the interview of Dr. Stakic. When we complete the transcript, I will have another exhibit of the 15 minutes or so that are most relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. So we limit it to the one minute and eight or whatever it was we saw here in the courtroom. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then this portion of this video is admitted into evidence as S240. May I ask the parties, did you receive this Chamber's decision on Defence request to exclude evidence as inadmissible?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did, Your Honour, but I have to admit that I haven't read it yet. I really didn't have time. I was preparing this witness, so -- but as I understood, the documents were admitted into the evidence, and I think that we will ask your permission to appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Will you or do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We just discussed this matter and we are aware that this would be your conclusion. We discussed this issue beforehand and, therefore, we decide as follows: Under Rule 73 of -- sorry, the right to be heard for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, but I have nothing to say, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then under Rule 73(B), the version of 1 May 2002, certification is granted because the decision involves an issue that would significantly affect the outcome of the trial and the further proceedings. It is important for the Trial Chamber whether or not this Trial Chamber can indeed work on the basis of also these photocopies included in the 81 documents. And furthermore, this might have an impact on the expertise requested on the handwriting and the authenticity of some documents. Therefore, an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber may materially advance the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then after having heard the information on the health condition of Dr. Stakic, we -- let's try to proceed. And please let us be informed on that, what happens in Banja Luka. The trial stays adjourned until further notice. Please, all the participants stand by. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of August, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.55 p.m.,
